focused_mathematical_findings.supplier_distinctions: Current def-pathwise-differentiable-functional defines a continuous linear score derivative on the closed span of designated one-sided DQM paths. def-asymptotically-linear-estimator-and-influence-function defines a centered L2 empirical expansion. The robust functional definition mentions both only in Remarks to distinguish them from its own right point-contamination derivative. It explicitly does not assert that gross-error paths are DQM and does not invoke Riesz, LAN, local-alternative regularity or estimator attainment.
focused_mathematical_findings.gross_error_supplier: Current def-gross-error-path gives (1-epsilon)F+epsilon H on one measurable space and specializes H=delta_x; it does not promise a uniform-in-H derivative remainder. The robust functional explicitly requires the small right path to remain in its domain.
focused_mathematical_findings.m_location: The current theorem assumes finite integral of |psi(y-theta)|, psi C1, one common integrable majorant for |psi_prime(y-t)| over an interval, and A=integral psi_prime(y-theta) nonzero. The mean-value theorem bounds difference quotients; dominated convergence proves J C1. Apply finite-dimensional IFT to H_x(e,t)=(1-e)J(t)+e psi(x-t), extended algebraically to real e near0, with H_t=-A and H_e=psi(x-theta). The right derivative is psi(x-theta)/A. This is pointwise in x; no uniform remainder or choice selection is invoked.
focused_mathematical_findings.median: Positive continuous local density gives an invertible cdf near the lower median. For x<m use F(q_e)=(1/2-e)/(1-e), yielding derivative -1/(2f(m)); for x>m use F(q_e)=1/[2(1-e)], yielding +1/(2f(m)). At x=m the cdf jump straddles1/2 and the lower median stays m, so the literal right derivative is0. The conventional indicator formula is retained only F-almost everywhere, and the sensitivity is1/(2f(m)).
focused_mathematical_findings.breakdown_and_examples: The first-unbounded-replacement-count convention gives sample mean1/n and odd sample median(r+1)/(2r+1). These are fixed-sample claims distinct from influence derivatives. The counterexample functional agrees with the median along a one-point-contamination path of a continuous uniform law because its trigger needs two distinct far atoms, giving bounded IF. At a clean odd sample in[-1,1], one replacement cannot trigger it; two replacements M,2M do, giving exact2/n breakdown for n>=5. Countable Choice is explicitly retained only through its Lebesgue measure suppliers.
